title: The Belly and the Members
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: The Members of the Body once rebelled against the Belly. "You," they said to the Belly, "live in luxury and sloth, and never do a stroke of work; while we not only have to do all the hard work there is to be done, but are actually your slaves and have to minister to all your wants. Now, we will do so no longer, and you can shift for yourself for the future."

They were as good as their word, and left the Belly to starve. The result was just what might have been expected: the whole Body soon began to fail, and the Members and all shared in the general collapse. And then they saw too late how foolish they had been.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who rebels against the Belly?
options: The other organs of the head
A group of neighboring bodies
The Members of the Body
The Belly's own servants

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Members accuse the Belly of doing?
options: Living in luxury and sloth without doing any work
Eating more than its fair share of food
Refusing to grow along with the rest of the body
Complaining constantly about the Members' efforts

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Members say they are forced to be?
options: The Belly's equals in every respect
The Belly's masters from now on
The Belly's teachers in hard work
The Belly's slaves, ministering to all its wants

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Members decide the Belly must do from now on?
options: Do all the work alone
Shift for itself
Apologize to each Member individually
Share its food equally with everyone

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens once the Members stop serving the Belly?
options: The Belly quickly finds another way to eat
The Members grow stronger without the Belly
The whole Body begins to fail
Nothing changes for either the Belly or the Members

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who suffers in the general collapse of the Body?
options: The Members and all
Only the Belly itself
Only the hands and feet
No one, since the Belly recovered quickly

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does starving the Belly end up harming the Members as well?
options: The Members are punished separately by an outside force
The Belly secretly withholds food even after being fed again
The Members misunderstood the Belly's true function from the start
The Members depend on the Belly's role even though its work is less visible than theirs

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what mistaken assumption do the Members make about the Belly's role?
options: They assume the Belly wants to take over control of the Body
They assume the Belly contributes nothing of real value to the whole Body
They assume the Belly is trying to starve them on purpose
They assume the Belly can survive without any of the Members

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "sloth" mean in "live in luxury and sloth"?
options: Wealth
Illness
Laziness
Anger

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Every part of a working whole depends on the others, even when one part's contribution is less visible
Hard workers should always be rewarded more than those who seem idle
Bodies function best when every part works completely independently
It is wise to refuse cooperation with anyone who seems unproductive

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Members say they must do that the Belly does not?
options: All the resting there is to be done
All the growing there is to be done
All the deciding there is to be done
All the hard work there is to be done

questions.prompt: According to the passage, do the Members actually follow through on their threat?
options: No, they quickly changed their minds
Yes, they were as good as their word
Yes, but only for a single day
No, the Belly convinced them not to

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Members leave the Belly to do?
options: Rest quietly
Find its own food elsewhere
Starve
Apologize on its own

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the outcome described as "just what might have been expected"?
options: Starving the Belly was always going to weaken the entire Body it feeds
The Members had been warned in advance by someone wiser
The Belly had threatened this outcome from the beginning
No one could have predicted such a result at all

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what do the Members finally realize "too late"?
options: That the Belly had been secretly helping them all along in another way
That another Member was truly to blame for the rebellion
That the Belly had never actually stopped working
That the Belly's role was necessary for their own survival too

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "minister to" mean in "minister to all your wants"?
options: To argue against someone's wishes
To attend to or provide for someone's needs
To ignore someone's requests
To report someone to an authority

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The Belly and the Members work out a fair division of labor
The Members successfully replace the Belly's function on their own
The Members starve the Belly to punish its apparent idleness, and the whole Body suffers as a result
The Belly apologizes and begins doing more visible work
